explanation: Use the fast branch when its size and polynomial-value conditions hold, and the explicit finite original-triple fallback otherwise; both branches have the same exact decision specification. This theorem provides one universal fixed-program decision contract, including the fast and finite fallback branches.
theorem_title: The complete hybrid program decides distinct-index integer 3SUM
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumHybrid.program_meets {lim : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Limits} {κ src n U free d : ℕ}
    (x : Fin n→ℤ) (μ : ℕ→ℤ) (hn : 0<n)
    (H : (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumHybrid.need κ n U).Ok lim free d)
    (hsrc : src+n≤free) (hinput : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Seg μ src (List.ofFn x))
    (hx : ∀ i, |x i|≤(U : ℤ)) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Meets lim (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumHybrid.program κ) 542 d [n,U,src,free] μ (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightThreeSumHybrid.time κ n U)
      (fun r ν => (r=0 ∨ r=1) ∧ (r=1 ↔ _root_.ThreeSum.Coloring.DistinctZeroSum x) ∧ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Kept μ ν free) := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
For natural exponent $\kappa$, a nonempty length-$n$ integer input $x$ bounded by $U$, and input memory stored before the free pointer, assume the complete hybrid resource predicate. Procedure 542 of the fixed program returns $r\in\{0,1\}$ such that $$r=1\iff\exists\text{ three distinct input indices whose values sum to }0.$$ It takes at most the defined hybrid time and preserves memory below the free pointer.

This theorem provides one universal fixed-program decision contract, including the fast and finite fallback branches.
